podWireStatus.description: The pod->control-plane WebSocket event status vocabulary and how it folds onto `status` above. The pod agent spells these and Go translates them before XADD. Not itself on this stream — the translated event is.

reservedStage.description: RESERVED stage name with contract force: an event whose stage is exactly this is about the WHOLE job, not a task, and the control plane sets terminal job state from it (internal/jobs ApplyEvent). Every other value is an opaque engine task name. Declared here because it was a magic string on both sides, constrained by nothing.

event.description: One stage-progress event on the shared events stream. TWO producers: the Python worker (per engine task) and the Go control plane (which folds typed pod WebSocket event frames onto the same stream). Consumer is the Go control plane. stage is a free string (the engine's task name) so adding/removing/renaming a stage does NOT bump this contract; status is a closed vocab Go branches on. DISCRIMINATOR: event vs manifest on the one stream is decided by the presence of `stage` — see manifest.schema.json.

capacity.description: opaque pod capacity snapshot (for example rank_lanes/fetch_workers), preserved independently from reason

corr_id.description: address of the pod sub-job/terminal inside a shared session lane

op.description: pod operation name, when the runner reports one

optional.description: whether a pod step may fail without failing its chain

origin.description: present only on control-plane-normalized pod events; consumers must use this marker instead of guessing from stage

outputs.description: pod output manifest, preserved as structured JSON rather than hidden in reason

session_id.description: pod-lane session that carried this event; optional for non-pod producers

skipped.description: optional pod step ids skipped on a terminal

stage.description: engine task name (e.g. head_motion), or the reserved value in $defs/reservedStage for the overall job

step.description: pod operation step id; preserved separately from human-readable reason

steps.description: completed pod step ids on a terminal

timeline.description: opaque end-to-end transport timeline. Go preserves the full tree; producers own its inner schema.

timings.description: opaque pod timing tree, relayed without a Go-side field mirror

event.title: MontageEvent

allOf.$comment: render_final renders FROM the FE-mutated plan (TWO_TIER_RENDER §5.3) — a render_final with no plan would silently render the pre-edit out/*.json and diverge from what the user previewed. Guard it in the contract, not deep in the render.

job.description: Go control plane -> Python worker. The envelope a worker pulls from Redis to run one job. type is one of scenario|plan|render_preview|render_final|palette|edit (RENDER_STAGE_MAP §5). The dev turnkey monolith is type=plan with params.turnkey=true. params AND plan are OPAQUE to Go (engine-owned; validated worker-side); only the envelope is the cross-language contract.

brand.description: channel brand slug (engine resolves brands/<brand>/). Go-owned, derived from projects.brand_id. Replaces the worker's hardcoded brand seed. OPTIONAL — absent on local-dev jobs built without the control plane, where the worker falls back to active_brand() (env BRAND).

channel.description: Redis pub/sub channel for events + manifest

chain_id.description: identity of ONE montage RUN across its plan/render_preview/render_final jobs. job_id is minted per STAGE, so before this the run had no name and the three stages' work prefixes were siblings under the tenant root — a stale run's files merged into a fresh one by mtime. OPTIONAL: a v7-shaped envelope still validates and consumers fall back to `chain_id or job_id`, reproducing the 3-segment prefix exactly — that fallback IS the migration for jobs already queued.

job_token.description: OPAQUE per-job bearer token the control plane mints at dispatch; the worker exports it (MONTY_JOB_TOKEN) for keyless /internal/llm calls. Closes the mint-never-wired gap.

music_recent.description: Go-owned anti-repeat seed: recent track relpaths for this (tenant, brand), most-recent-first, read from the control-plane music_history table. The worker feeds these to music_select's recency penalty INSTEAD of brands/<brand>/music_history.json (now a local-dev fallback). OPTIONAL — absent on local-dev jobs (worker falls back to the file).

output_prefix.description: R2 key prefix for KEPT deliverables, project-scoped: deliverables/<tenant>/<project>/

params.description: OPAQUE to Go. Engine montage knobs (pace/broll/director-model/...). Worker validates against engine-side params schema. Adding a knob does NOT bump this contract.

plan.description: OPAQUE to Go, like params. The FE-mutated PreviewPlan (swaps/music/transitions/mograph text) — the SSOT input to render_final so preview and final render from ONE plan (TWO_TIER_RENDER §5.3). Present on render_final; absent elsewhere. Worker validates its shape against the engine PreviewPlan schema. May carry an optional `layers` control field (which composition layers render_final (re)builds: broll/captions/mograph/logo/cover/watermark, or absent = all) — a targeted PATCH; engine-validated against scripts/layer_set.py, still opaque to Go (Go only mirrors the closed key set).

render_tier.description: which RenderProfile the render stages bake to: preview=540x960 proxy clean plate (render_base), final=1080x1920 master (render_final). OPTIONAL — absent on non-render jobs (analyze/resolve) and on the monolith unless it targets a tier.

scenario.description: The APPROVED preproduction script the montage renders from. Go seeds it from the scenarios table (the durable per-(tenant, project) store); the worker writes it to projects/<slug>/scenario.md so the director reads it unchanged. OPTIONAL — absent on upload-only jobs and on type=scenario generation jobs.

music_mood.description: mood/energy/texture hint the Director Brief reads

source_key.description: The raw recording's own R2 object key (uploads/<tenant>/<uid>-<name>, minted by POST /api/uploads and already validated by ownedKey). source_url is a ~24h capability: it cannot be re-minted, HEADed or stored, so a stage that must hand the recording to a keyless pod op has to re-upload a second copy under work_prefix — the box paying a full download+upload of the recording per stage. With the KEY the engine presigns the object where it already sits and the media never crosses the control-plane box (docs/TRANSPORT_ARCHITECTURE.md). OPTIONAL — absent on local-dev jobs built without the control plane and on any submit that named a raw source_url; consumers fall back to source_url.

source_url.description: presigned R2 GET for the raw recording

type.description: scenario = preproduction script (ensemble); plan = brain, everything up to spec (replaces analyze+resolve; params.turnkey=true runs the dev monolith); render_preview = pod 540x960 proxy (render_tier=preview) — TERMINAL for the first view: its done-manifest means the viewer plan is on the store and playable; palette = the CONTINUATION render_preview chains into (render_tier=preview), which re-emits that SAME plan with the editor's swap-palette proxies and nothing else; render_final = 1080p master from the FE-mutated plan; edit = delta mutation (plan-patch / trims / NL). scenario+edit are not yet executable by the engine. FE CONTRACT ON `palette`: it is a booked stage-job like any other (own job row, chain edge, progress events, terminal manifest), so a client polling the submitted id sees type=palette the moment the preview is ready — the mere EXISTENCE of a palette stage in the chain is the statement that render_preview finished. While it runs the plan is already usable, with palette rows carrying no `previewSrc` (the player reads `previewSrc ?? src` and plays the master — the same degrade a failed proxy chain has always produced). When it reaches status=done the client re-GETs GET /api/jobs/{submitted_id}/plan, which always serves the NEWEST plan in the run.

work_prefix.description: R2 key prefix for the job's WORKING SET (source+intermediates+ALL candidates): work/<tenant>/<chain>/<job>/ when chain_id is present, else the legacy job-scoped work/<tenant>/<job>/. Lives until the user commits, then GC'd (one prefix delete per run) — enables cheap re-edits without re-sourcing.

job.title: MontageJob

manifest.description: Python worker -> Go control plane on completion. The deliverables a finished job produced in R2 (master/shorts/cover/thumbnail) — what Go meters for quota and hands the user via presigned URLs. Intermediates/sidecars are NOT in the boundary. DISCRIMINATOR: event and manifest share ONE Redis stream and are told apart by the presence of `stage` (contracts.IsEvent / cmd/api fold). That rule is only safe because this schema is closed AND declares no `stage` property — adding one here would make every manifest decode as an event and no job would ever reach a terminal state. examples/invalid/manifest.with-stage.json is the golden that holds it.

music_track.description: repo-relative path of the music track the worker committed for this job. The control plane appends it to the music_history table (anti-repeat, per (tenant, brand)). OPTIONAL — absent when the job used no music or reused a sticky prior pick.

scenario.description: The preproduction script a type=scenario job generated. The control plane persists it to scenarios.body (per (tenant, project), a new draft version). OPTIONAL — present only on a done scenario job.

manifest.title: MontageManifest

pod_enqueue_ack.description: Control-plane acknowledgement for one POST /internal/pod-jobs Redis enqueue. The bounds use the control-plane Unix clock; attempt_id is absent because attempts begin at claim.
pod_enqueue_ack.title: PodEnqueueAck

attemptId.description: Claim identity minted atomically with Redis reserve and stable across socket replay.

timeline.description: Opaque terminal/step timeline preserved unchanged by Go.

podResult.description: Full infer/result body is stored immutable and interpreted by the box. Go validates routing/status/correlation only.

timeline.description: Opaque terminal timeline preserved unchanged by Go.

streamId.description: Fresh for one pod process, stable across reconnects.

pod_stream.description: Strict pod->control-plane frame on the sole pod transport. Every frame carries a pod-monotonic send stamp; terminal frames echo the atomic claim attempt.
pod_stream.title: PodStreamClientFrame

target_worker_id.description: Control-plane-only warm-up routing fence. The API strips it before the WebSocket payload; a fleet worker may claim the stored envelope only when its identity matches.

pod_stream_server.description: Strict control-plane->pod frame on the sole pod transport.
pod_stream_server.title: PodStreamServerFrame

pod_token.description: Cross-language HMAC token payload. aud separates submitter tokens from physical pod workers; omitted aud is legacy-only and cannot access shared-fleet transport.
pod_token.title: Monty pod bearer claims

pod_transport_receipt.description: Authoritative control-plane timeline for one corr+attempt+pod-stream delivery. Persisted after socket write and completed by the pod's job_ack.
pod_transport_receipt.title: PodTransportReceipt

publish_job.description: Go control plane -> Python worker, on the SEPARATE monty:jobs:publish lane (redis_keys.json routing: type=publish). It is NOT a MontageJob — publish-on-behalf carries per-user OAuth grants and presigned deliverables, and it crossed the seam for a whole milestone described by nothing: Go typed a struct, the worker read two keys off a raw dict, and no schema knew the shape. Correlation fields sit top-level; the pinned creative contract is nested under params (opaque HERE exactly as MontageJob.params is opaque to Go — the worker validates it against publish_job_models.PublishJob, extra=forbid). REQUIRED is what the CONSUMER cannot work without: an address (job_id) and the params blob; everything else Go stamps for attribution and the worker may ignore.

callback.description: VESTIGIAL, like MontageJob.callback: the worker ignores it and XADDs to the events stream. Declared because Go stamps it.

job_id.description: the montage job whose deliverables are being published — the id every event/manifest on this lane is attributed to

params.description: OPAQUE here. The pinned publish contract (platforms/tokens/deliverables/publish_meta/funnel_url), validated worker-side by publish_job_models.PublishJob. A knob added there does NOT bump this contract.

schema_version.description: OPTIONAL on this lane: the worker addresses and validates the envelope without it, so requiring it would reject in-flight envelopes for nothing. Go stamps it so a version skew is visible in the payload.

publish_job.title: PublishEnvelope
